notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend exists and no hardware was run. The upstream-sim path was not used: ExampleEnvSim launches an external example_robot_server with roslaunch (example_env.py:228) and reset/step talk to that gRPC server (example_env.py:89-99 and :128-133), whose side is in robo-gym-robot-servers (README.md:102-103), not in this clone. The fake is therefore the package stand-in: it mirrors ExampleEnv's Box spaces (two action elements from -1.0 to 1.0; four unbounded observation elements), options.position, the 300-step limit and the reward/done rule, with placeholder kinematics for the server state. The sim backend (gymnasium.make('ExampleEnvSim-v0')) was not run; it needs the upstream package and an external robot server. NOT COVERED: the external robot server and its ROS/Gazebo dynamics, contact/actuator/sensor/noise models, rendering, and any comparison of the fake with upstream or a physical device. The fidelity contract declares F0, timestep_ms 0 (the clone declares no fixed timestep; the external server owns it), realtime_factor 0, clock lockstep, reset full and no snapshot/restore. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer inputs (seed twice, ticks and action.values). There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
